---
title: "Slide Animations — usage guide"
subtitle: "A compact API for presenter-controlled explanations"
---

## Design contract

- Reveal.js owns all slide and fragment navigation.
- CSS handles simple movement and visual emphasis.
- JS handles coupled numerical or geometric state.
- Magic Move handles compatible SVG, code and equation transitions.
- No global timeline, rendering framework, autoplay or mandatory animation.

## Install in Quarto

```bash
quarto add Lawrence-lugs/revealjs-slide-animations
quarto add emilhvitfeldt/quarto-revealjs-magic-move
```

```yaml
format:
  revealjs:
    revealjs-plugins: [slide-animations, magic-move]
    theme: [white, slides.scss]
```

Magic Move is optional. Omit it from the plugin list if you do not need it.

## Install once at the Quarto project root

```text
workspace/
  _quarto.yml
  _extensions/
    Lawrence-lugs/slide-animations/
  lectures/
    week01.qmd
    week02.qmd
```

From the directory containing the active `_quarto.yml`, install the extension and run `quarto render lectures/week01.qmd`. Enable the plugin in that deck's front matter, or in project metadata for all Reveal decks. Quarto searches from the document directory up to its project root. A nested `_quarto.yml` creates a separate root; a workspace without a recognized project is not a shared extension installation. Inspect with `quarto inspect lectures/week01.qmd`; do not copy extensions beside every lecture. If using independent nested projects, install once per actual project.

## Use in native Reveal.js

Copy the two files from the extension directory, load CSS and JS after Reveal, register the plugin.

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="motion.css">
<script src="motion.js"></script>
<script>
Reveal.initialize({plugins:[SlideAnimations]});
</script>
```

The exported global is `SlideAnimations`. No additional runtime dependencies.

## Highlight existing text

```markdown
[This term matters]{.fragment .custom .sa-highlight}
```

[This term matters]{.fragment .custom .sa-highlight}

[Then this term matters]{.fragment .custom .sa-highlight}

Both remain readable. Only the current fragment changes color.

## Drawing and flow

```html
<path class="fragment sa-draw" pathLength="1"
      d="M10 40 H250" stroke="currentColor"
      fill="none" />
<path class="fragment sa-flow" d="M10 90 H250"
      stroke="currentColor" fill="none" />
```

<svg class="sa-svg" viewBox="0 0 600 120" style="max-height:130px"><path class="fragment sa-draw sa-slow" pathLength="1" d="M40 30 H560" stroke="#3977a8" stroke-width="5" fill="none"/><path class="fragment sa-flow" d="M40 90 H560" stroke="#c67e6a" stroke-width="5" fill="none"/></svg>

Draw uses normalized path length. Flow is passive CSS, paused when the slide is inactive or its fragment hidden.

## Layout morphs: use Auto-Animate

```markdown
## Step A {auto-animate="true"}

<div data-id="block">Same object</div>

## Step B {auto-animate="true"}

<div data-id="block" style="width:70%">Same object</div>
```

Keep stable `data-id` values. Use a new slide for an actual layout change; use fragments for incremental content on one layout.

## General numerical interpolation

```js
const m = SlideAnimations;
m.lerp(0, 10, .5); // 5
m.interpolate({x:0,y:2}, {x:10,y:4}, .5);
const cancel = m.tween({
  from: 0, to: 1, duration: 500,
  update: p => draw(p)
});
// cancel() interrupts the animation
```

Numbers, equal-length arrays and plain objects with stable keys interpolate recursively. Non-numeric leaves switch at the endpoint. Do not use tween to create a presentation timeline.

## Bind state to presenter steps

```js
SlideAnimations.bindState('#diagram', {
  initial: {x: 0},
  steps: [
    {index: 0, state: {x: 1}},
    {index: 1, state: {x: 2}}
  ],
  duration: 650,
  render: ({x}, element) => update(element, x)
});
```

Create corresponding native fragments with explicit indices. Register after Reveal's ready event. The API returns an unbind function. Navigation reconstructs the selected state; interrupted transitions start from the current interpolated state.

## A state-driven example

<svg id="state-demo" class="sa-svg" viewBox="0 0 600 130" style="max-height:150px"><path d="M50 65 H550" stroke="currentColor" stroke-opacity=".25" stroke-width="4"/><circle r="14" cy="65" cx="50" fill="#c67e6a"/><text x="50" y="115" font-size="19">0%</text></svg>
<span class="fragment sa-trigger" data-fragment-index="0"></span>
<span class="fragment sa-trigger" data-fragment-index="1"></span>
<script>
document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded',()=>{
 const init=()=>SlideAnimations.bindState('#state-demo',{initial:{p:0},steps:[{index:0,state:{p:.5}},{index:1,state:{p:1}}],render:({p},el)=>{el.querySelector('circle').setAttribute('cx',50+500*p);el.querySelector('text').textContent=Math.round(p*100)+'%';}});
 if(Reveal.isReady())init();else Reveal.on('ready',init);
});
</script>

Click forward or backward. The marker and numeric label derive from the same driver.

## SVG utilities

```js
SlideAnimations.attrs(circle, {cx: 100, cy: 50});
SlideAnimations.moveAlongPath(circle, path, .5);
```

The path helper targets SVG circle/ellipse coordinates in the same coordinate space. For arbitrary objects or differing transforms, calculate the appropriate coordinates yourself. For a time-domain plot, calculate the point from the physical time parameter rather than arc length.

## Parameter-driven plots

Use the existing plotting library to render the axes, labels, legends and initial traces. For Matplotlib, assign stable artist IDs with `line.set_gid("my-line")`, save as inline SVG and export the affine data-to-SVG transform. Use `bindState` and `samplePath` to regenerate only the paths from the interpolated parameter.

```js
const d = SlideAnimations.samplePath(
  x => Math.sin(x + phase),
  {from:0, to:2*Math.PI, samples:181,
   map:[xOrigin,yOrigin,xScale,yScale]}
);
path.setAttribute("d", d);
```

This helper assumes affine (linear) axes. For log/polar axes or arbitrary curves, use the plotting library's own transform or a custom render callback. The Matplotlib example contains the full Python-to-SVG mapping. Never interpolate endpoint waveform geometry to represent a phase shift.

## Animate Mermaid without changing its layout

Wrap the original Mermaid cell in a uniquely identified div. Assign semantic classes in Mermaid, for example `class F sa-fetch`. Keep the full graph in one cell to avoid re-layout at every click. Inspect the rendered SVG to identify edges. If a Quarto-rendered HTML label clips, add `.sa-mermaid` to the diagram wrapper. Set `--sa-mermaid-max-width` on that wrapper to override the inline width cap and verify the labels still fit their nodes.

```js
SlideAnimations.bindElements("#diagram", {
  targets: {a:".node.sa-a", b:".node.sa-b"},
  initial: {show:["a"]},
  steps: [
    {index:0,state:{show:["a","b"]}},
    {index:1,state:{focus:["b"]}}
  ]
});
```

The API also accepts a raw JSON script with `type="application/json" data-sa-elements` and a `scope` selector, as in the example deck. It waits for late-rendered SVG and reapplies state when the diagram is replaced.

## Demonstrate a transformation {#document-conversion}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="45%"}
**Source page**

```markdown
# Bias
[Notes](notes.md)
```

<div class="fragment custom sa-focus-plain" data-fragment-index="0">Move the heading into metadata.</div>
<div class="fragment custom sa-focus-plain" data-fragment-index="1">Retarget the link to the converted page.</div>
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
**Output page**

<div id="conversion-output" data-sa-qa>

```text
# Bias
[Notes](notes.md)
```

</div>
:::
::::

<script>
document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', () => {
  const bind = () => {
    const output = document.querySelector('#conversion-output code');
    const source = '# Bias\n[Notes](notes.md)';
    const metadata = '---\ntitle: Bias\n---\n';
    SlideAnimations.bindState(output, {
      initial: {text: source},
      steps: [
        {index: 0, state: {text: metadata + '[Notes](notes.md)'}},
        {index: 1, state: {text: metadata + '[Notes](notes.qmd)'}}
      ],
      duration: 0,
      render: state => { output.textContent = state.text; }
    });
  };
  if (Reveal.isReady()) bind();
  else Reveal.on('ready', bind);
});
</script>

## Element-state API

Each step is a complete state, not a delta.

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| show | Only these target names visible; omit for all |
| focus | Dim all other visible targets; omit for no dim |
| flow | Apply passive dashed animation to the named SVG paths |

Use ordinary fragments with matching indices as triggers. Select edge labels separately when present; flow applies only to paths. Inspect `data-sa-ready` and `data-sa-missing` on the wrapper: unresolved targets leave the diagram static rather than half-hidden. Do not rely on generated numeric IDs or text matching.

## Magic Move: SVG plots

```markdown
## Before {.magic-move}

[Python cell producing an SVG]

## After {.magic-move}

[Python cell producing the next SVG]
```

```yaml
jupyter: python3
fig-format: svg
```

Set a fixed Matplotlib `svg.hashsalt`, identical figure size and axis limits, and use the same plot colors and element order.

See the examples deck for the Seaborn geometric transition and the separate parameter-driven Matplotlib example. Magic Move is not suitable for exact phase shifts or other physically meaningful intermediate states. Verify both endpoints and intermediate frames; if any trace fails to move, replace the morph with a state-driven update.

## Magic Move: code and equations

````markdown
::: magic-move

```python
x = 1
```

```python
x = 1 + 2
```

:::
````

For equations, use consecutive display-math blocks inside the same div. Test the exact renderer and content you use; token matching is heuristic.

## Magic Move limitations

- Matplotlib scatter markers often use SVG `<use>` glyphs, which may not morph.
- Clipping IDs and transformed ancestor groups can break correspondence.
- Dynamic SVG created after Reveal is ready may not be picked up.
- Diagram topology changes may require explicit semantic state mapping.
- A visually correct fallback is preferable to a misleading morph.

## Style inheritance

```css
.reveal {
  --sa-duration: 360ms;
  --sa-distance: .65em;
  --sa-accent: #c67e6a;
  --sa-dim: .38;
  --sa-card-gap: .35em;
}
```

No global font family, heading reset, column override or background. Card colors derive from current text color and accent. Use `.sa-fast` or `.sa-slow` on individual fragments to override duration.

## Agent workflow

1. Read the deck, identify teaching intent and verify formulas.
2. Identify one focal change per step; keep reading targets stationary.
3. Choose the simplest native or library primitive.
4. Implement explicit fragment states and test reversibility.
5. Inspect settled and intermediate states; remove decorative motion.

Skill: `.agents/skills/revealjs-slide-animations/SKILL.md`.

## Build and verify

```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt
npm install
bash scripts/build.sh
npm test
npx playwright install chromium
npm run test:browser
```

Verify forward, backward, direct jumps, rapid interruption and reduced motion. Browser tests are not substitutes for inspecting the slides visually.
